Thermal runaway risk is negligible (Da_thermal << 0.1) due to the mild exotherm of condensation, but pressure management is critical. Both candidates currently have a BPR set to 1.0 bar, which is dangerously inadequate for a system operating at 80°C with acetic acid (P_vap ~ 1.0 bar) plus flow resistance. The BPR must be raised to at least 3.0 bar to ensure a robust safety margin against overpressure and pump fluctuations. Material compatibility is acceptable with PFA, provided the system is fully sealed to prevent acid vapor leaks. Hazard flags include corrosive acetic acid and potential skin irritation; standard PPE and closed-system handling are mandatory. The safety landscape is dominated by the use of hot acetic acid (80°C), which presents significant corrosion and vapor pressure risks. While thermal runaway risk is negligible (Da_thermal << 0.1), the material compatibility is critical: PFA is mandatory to resist hot acetic acid, as PTFE is opaque (blocking light if photochemical, though this is thermal condensation, PFA is still preferred for chemical resistance) and FEP may have lower temperature limits. The current BPR setting of 1.0 bar is critically inadequate for both candidates, as the vapor pressure of acetic acid at 80°C is ~0.35 bar, leaving insufficient margin for pressure drops and safety. BPR must be raised to at least 2.0 bar (recommended 3.0 bar) to ensure liquid phase stability and safety. Hazard management requires closed-system handling of acetic acid vapors (corrosive/irritant) and appropriate PPE.
